lead.title: Powerful Thanksgiving storm lashes the East Coast as Philadelphia parade drops balloons
lead.deck: Forecasters warned of heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding from the Mid-Atlantic into New England on Thanksgiving morning, disrupting travel and forcing changes to holiday events.
paragraphs: A strong coastal storm was expected to bring heavy rain, damaging wind gusts and significant coastal flooding to the Eastern Seaboard on Thursday, with federal forecasters warning that Thanksgiving morning travel, parades and outdoor events could be affected from the Carolinas through southern New England. NOAA’s Weather Prediction Center said the system would track up the coast during the holiday, while local forecasters in the Philadelphia region warned of soaking rain and the risk of downed trees and power outages.

In Philadelphia, the 107th Thanksgiving Day Parade was still scheduled to proceed Thursday morning, but organizers said the giant helium balloons would not fly because of the wind forecast. The route and a broad set of road closures remained in place across Center City and the Benjamin Franklin Parkway. At the Shore, Atlantic City officials warned of flooding around the morning high tide as the storm pushed water toward the coast.

stories.title: Vance says Huang does not need a pardon as Washington scrutiny continues
stories.deck: The vice president’s remarks kept the Nvidia controversy in the political arena a day after the company’s leadership restoration.
paragraphs: Vice President JD Vance said Wednesday that Jensen Huang would not need a pardon, a comment that underscored continuing political scrutiny around Nvidia’s chief executive even after his formal return to the company. The statement followed President Trump’s separate suggestion that a pardon was theoretically available but unnecessary.

The episode has kept a corporate governance matter entangled with national politics at a time when Nvidia remains central to U.S. debates over AI, export controls and industrial policy. It also suggests congressional attention to the company is unlikely to fade simply because its board settled the immediate leadership question.
stories.new_development: The new development is Vance’s public statement that Huang does not need a pardon, extending the political fallout after Nvidia reinstated him on Nov. 23.

stories.title: Philadelphia’s Thanksgiving parade marches on, but without balloons
stories.deck: The annual procession remained on schedule despite wind and rain, with broad closures around Center City and the Parkway.
paragraphs: Philadelphia’s Thanksgiving Day Parade was set to proceed Thursday morning despite a poor weather forecast, but organizers said the event’s helium balloons would stay grounded because of high winds. The parade was scheduled to run from 8:30 a.m. to noon, and city officials warned drivers to expect extensive road closures and SEPTA detours around the route.

Closures began earlier in the week and expanded overnight into Thursday, including on John F. Kennedy Boulevard, 20th Street, Market Street, Kelly Drive and the Benjamin Franklin Parkway. Roads tied to the event were expected to reopen by Thursday afternoon as cleanup was completed.
stories.new_development: The new development is that parade organizers said the event would go on despite the storm, but the balloons were removed from the plan because of expected high winds.

stories.title: Sherrill declares a statewide emergency ahead of Thanksgiving storm
stories.deck: New Jersey’s governor put all 21 counties under a state of emergency effective Wednesday evening as severe weather approached.
paragraphs: Gov. Mikie Sherrill declared a state of emergency for all 21 New Jersey counties effective at 6 p.m. Wednesday in anticipation of severe weather tied to the Thanksgiving coastal storm. The order came as forecasters warned of strong winds, flooding and hazardous travel conditions during the holiday.

The declaration gives state agencies broader authority to coordinate response and pre-position resources. For South Jersey communities already watching tidal flooding and wind impacts, it formalized the state’s storm posture before the worst conditions were expected Thursday morning.

stories.title: Philadelphia backs holiday markets and a Market East lighting push
stories.deck: The city said it will fund vendor support, performances and corridor decorations through the holiday season.
paragraphs: Philadelphia officials said Wednesday that the city is putting money behind several holiday initiatives, including support for nonprofit groups helping small vendors sell at Christmas Village, live performance programming at local businesses and a lighting-and-decoration campaign along Market East. The effort runs through the holiday shopping season and includes a walkable display corridor from City Hall to Independence Hall starting Dec. 3.

The city said $46,125 would help cover booth costs and support services for 19 local vendors at Christmas Village through partner organizations. The announcement also ties into the Parker administration’s broader effort to reactivate Market East with visible public programming after a year dominated by debate over the corridor’s future.

stories.title: Philadelphia planning and art agencies reorganize staff
stories.deck: City officials said the changes are meant to streamline reviews and strengthen community planning work without layoffs.
paragraphs: The Philadelphia City Planning Commission and the Philadelphia Art Commission said they have reorganized 48 staff positions within the Department of Planning and Development, creating new work units and shifting responsibilities among teams. Officials said no employees were terminated as part of the reorganization.

The agencies described the move as an effort to restore community planning functions more clearly to the planning commission and clarify the art commission’s role as the city’s arts-and-culture planning authority. The change comes as development review, neighborhood planning and public-realm projects remain central issues in City Hall.

stories.title: Sherrill orders statewide literacy push in New Jersey schools
stories.deck: The executive order sets deadlines for a reading strategy, approved screening tools and a literacy coaching pilot.
paragraphs: Gov. Mikie Sherrill signed an executive order Monday directing the New Jersey Department of Education to expand evidence-based reading instruction, strengthen third-grade reading proficiency and narrow achievement gaps across the state. The order requires an early-literacy strategic plan within 90 days and a list of approved screening tools within 180 days.

It also calls for a review of instructional materials, stronger educator training and a regional literacy-coaching pilot. The administration framed the move as a statewide effort to build on earlier bipartisan literacy legislation and standardize what schools use to identify and respond to reading difficulties.

stories.title: Philadelphia certified its November election results on the county deadline
stories.deck: The board’s formal meeting completed the city’s canvass and sent certified returns on to the state.
paragraphs: Philadelphia’s Board of Elections met Monday to consider certification of the official returns from the Nov. 3 general election, in line with the county deadline set on the city’s election calendar. The certification step follows counting, verification and post-election review before submission to the Pennsylvania Department of State.

The meeting did not carry the drama of some recent election cycles, but it closed out a major administrative process in the state’s largest county. City officials had previously highlighted faster unofficial reporting on election night compared with the prior general election.
stories.new_development: The new development is that the board reached the scheduled Nov. 23 certification stage, completing the county’s formal canvass process.

stories.title: South Jersey towns prepare tree lightings and holiday markets
stories.deck: Communities across the region are opening the post-Thanksgiving season with civic events, markets and performances.
paragraphs: South Jersey municipalities and community groups are set to begin the holiday stretch with tree lightings, markets and town events after Thanksgiving, including programs in Mount Laurel, Haddonfield, Barrington and Haddon Heights. Organizers are advertising student performances, vendor markets, Santa visits and seasonal street events running from late November into December.

The calendar is largely civic rather than commercial, offering a snapshot of how town centers across the region use small-scale holiday programming to draw families and shoppers. Some towns are also pairing the events with parking changes and business-district promotions.

stories.title: NASA awards contract work for NOAA’s next-generation orbiting weather network
stories.deck: The federal agencies said Northrop Grumman won work on microwave sounder instruments for the NEON satellite program.
paragraphs: NASA said Monday that, acting on behalf of NOAA, it had awarded Northrop Grumman a contract for Sounder for Microwave-Based Applications instruments on NOAA’s Near Earth Orbit Network satellites. The award is part of the government’s long-term effort to refresh core weather-observation infrastructure in low Earth orbit.

The NEON program is meant to support future forecasting capacity by replacing aging space-based capabilities with newer instruments. Contracts like this tend to draw limited public attention at first, but they shape the quality and continuity of federal weather data for years.

stories.title: NASA seeks partners to design the first nuclear reactor for the Moon
stories.deck: The agency said it is looking for industry participation in a power system intended to support future lunar operations.
paragraphs: NASA said this week it is seeking partners to help design what it described as the first nuclear reactor for the Moon. The project is aimed at providing a durable power source for future lunar missions, where long nights, extreme conditions and distance from Earth make surface energy systems a central engineering problem.

The reactor effort fits into a broader push to prepare for sustained operations rather than short visits. NASA listed the partner search among its Nov. 23 science and agency updates, signaling that planning is advancing even if a flight-ready system remains years away.

stories.title: New NASA image update tracks an eruption that is extending Iwo Jima’s beach
stories.deck: A science update highlighted how volcanic activity is physically reshaping the island’s coastline.
paragraphs: NASA Science’s Nov. 24 roundup highlighted an eruption that has been extending the beach on Iwo Jima, offering a vivid example of how active geology can redraw coastlines on short timescales. The feature appeared in the agency’s daily science listings rather than as a major policy announcement, but it added a striking natural-history note to the week’s science news.

The item underscores the value of satellite and remote-observation programs in documenting changes in places that are difficult or hazardous to monitor up close. NASA’s science feed presented it alongside astronomy and planetary updates published the same day.

stories.title: Energy Department issues emergency order for Puerto Rico power supply
stories.deck: A federal emergency directive remains in effect through the end of the year as officials try to stabilize the island’s grid.
paragraphs: The U.S. Department of Energy’s list of 2026 emergency orders shows an order to the Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority effective from Nov. 18 through Dec. 31. Such 202(c) orders are used sparingly to keep electricity flowing during reliability emergencies when normal market or regulatory arrangements are not enough.

The posting offers a reminder that grid reliability remains a live federal concern well beyond mainland storm zones. It also comes as electricity supply and permitting have become more prominent national policy debates amid data-center growth and wider demand pressure.

stories.title: Eagles stop their slide with a 19-16 win over Pittsburgh
stories.deck: Philadelphia ended a seven-game losing streak behind defense, field goals and a late clinching throw from Joe Milton to DeVonta Smith.
paragraphs: The Eagles beat the Steelers 19-16 on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field, their first victory since Week 2 and a needed break in a difficult season. Team coverage said Philadelphia improved to 3-7 as Jake Elliott hit four field goals, Saquon Barkley scored on a 38-yard run and the defense produced five sacks against Aaron Rodgers.

The win does not erase the broader damage of the season, but it changes the tone heading into Thursday’s divisional game at Dallas. Philadelphia’s official schedule lists the Cowboys matchup for Thanksgiving afternoon.
stories.new_development: The new development is the Eagles’ 19-16 win over Pittsburgh on Nov. 22, which ended the team’s seven-game losing streak.

stories.title: Eagles head to Dallas for Thanksgiving afternoon kickoff
stories.deck: Philadelphia’s next test comes quickly, with a road division game scheduled for Thursday.
paragraphs: Philadelphia is scheduled to play at Dallas on Thursday, Nov. 26, with kickoff listed for 1:30 p.m. Pacific on the league schedule feed, or 4:30 p.m. in the Eastern time zone. The short turnaround follows the Eagles’ home win over Pittsburgh and gives them a chance to string together consecutive victories for the first time since early in the season.

Thanksgiving divisional games often reshape late-season storylines, and this one arrives with both rivalry weight and little recovery time. As of Thursday morning, the game was listed on schedule rather than as a completed result.

stories.title: 76ers beat Miami 111-104 behind LeBron’s first triple-double as a Sixer
stories.deck: Philadelphia rebounded from its loss to Portland with a home NBA Cup win Wednesday night.
paragraphs: The 76ers defeated the Heat 111-104 on Wednesday at Xfinity Mobile Arena, with LeBron James posting 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds for his first triple-double since joining Philadelphia. NBA.com’s game summary said Tyrese Maxey added 30 points as the Sixers improved their position after Monday’s 128-111 loss to Portland.
The result came with Joel Embiid again sidelined by illness and Jaylen Brown leaving after the first half with hamstring tightness. Philadelphia next travels to Indiana on Friday.

stories.title: Capitals score four late goals and beat the Flyers 7-3
stories.deck: Washington broke open a tight game in the third period, handing Philadelphia a lopsided road loss.
paragraphs: The Flyers lost 7-3 to the Capitals on Wednesday night after Washington scored four goals in a span of 2:48 late in the third period. NHL.com said the win snapped a five-game skid for the Capitals and turned a competitive game into a decisive defeat at Capital One Arena.

For Philadelphia, the result interrupted the momentum from earlier comeback-heavy performances and added another swing to an uneven stretch of the schedule. The official recap centered on Washington’s late burst rather than a prolonged Flyers collapse.

stories.title: This week’s sky note: November opened a run of three straight supermoons
stories.deck: NASA’s monthly skywatching guide said the full moon on Nov. 24 was the first in a sequence continuing through winter.
paragraphs: NASA’s monthly skywatching guide noted that the full moon of Nov. 24 was a supermoon, the first in a run of three consecutive months in which the full moon appears slightly larger and brighter than average because of the Moon’s distance from Earth. The agency encouraged viewers to look east around sunset to catch the effect, though it noted the visual difference is subtle.

The guide also bundled the supermoon with a month that included the Leonids, Taurids and a close Mars-Jupiter pairing. It was published earlier in November, but the timing of the full moon made it newly relevant this week.
